gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: The two sides finally ___ terms in the early hours of the morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Come to terms' is the fixed expression for reaching agreement.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a quick shower before leaving the gym.
gaps.explanation: have a shower is the standard British English collocation; 'made a shower' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.
